questions.questionText: Which Windows tool is used to view system event logs?

explanation.correct: Event Viewer shows application, security, and system logs.
explanation.incorrect: Task Manager shows processes; Device Manager manages hardware; Registry Editor edits the registry.
explanation.examTip: Use Event Viewer to troubleshoot system errors and warnings.

metadata.examObjective: 1.2: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: Match each Windows tool to its primary function.

explanation.correct: Task Manager = end processes; Device Manager = manage drivers; Event Viewer = logs.
explanation.incorrect: Mismatching functions indicates lack of familiarity.
explanation.examTip: These tools are commonly used for troubleshooting.

metadata.examObjective: 1.2: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.scenarioText: You are troubleshooting a Windows 11 system that is slow to boot.
questions.questionText: Which of the following tools can help identify startup issues? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: msconfig and Task Manager's Startup tab can disable startup programs.
explanation.incorrect: Disk Cleanup frees space but doesn't address startup; Get-Process shows processes.
explanation.examTip: Slow boot is often caused by too many startup programs.

metadata.examObjective: 1.4: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Windows OS troubleshooting tools

questions.questionText: Order the steps to perform a clean Windows 11 installation from a USB drive.

orderItems.text: Back up important data
Create a bootable USB drive with Windows 11 media
Boot from USB and select installation drive
Follow the installation wizard and complete setup

explanation.correct: 1: Backup, 2: Create USB, 3: Boot and select drive, 4: Install.
explanation.incorrect: Skipping backup can lead to data loss.
explanation.examTip: Always back up data before performing a clean install.

metadata.examObjective: 1.5: Given a scenario, install Windows OS upgrades and updates

questions.questionText: Which of the following are valid methods to update drivers in Windows? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Device Manager allows manual driver update; Windows Update may provide drivers.
explanation.incorrect: Registry and msconfig are not for driver updates.
explanation.examTip: Always get drivers from the manufacturer's website if possible.

metadata.examObjective: 1.2: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: Evaluate each statement about Windows backup types.

statements.text: A full backup backs up all selected files.
An incremental backup backs up files changed since the last full backup.
A differential backup backs up files changed since the last full backup.
Incremental backups require the full backup and all subsequent incrementals to restore.

explanation.correct: Full = all; incremental = changes since last incremental (not full); differential = since last full.
explanation.incorrect: Incremental is since last incremental, not last full.
explanation.examTip: Differential restores are faster than incremental.

metadata.examObjective: 1.7: Explain the importance of backups and recovery

questions.questionText: Select the Linux command that matches each description.

explanation.correct: ls lists, cd changes, grep searches.
explanation.incorrect: pwd shows current directory.
explanation.examTip: grep is powerful for searching logs.

metadata.examObjective: 1.10: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Linux commands

questions.questionText: Order the steps to use System Restore in Windows.

orderItems.text: Open System Properties and select System Restore
Choose a restore point before the issue occurred
Confirm the restore point and start the process
Wait for the system to restart and restore

explanation.correct: 1: Open System Restore, 2: Select restore point, 3: Confirm, 4: Restart.
explanation.incorrect: Skipping or wrong order can cause the restore to fail.
explanation.examTip: System Restore does not affect personal files.

metadata.examObjective: 1.6: Given a scenario, troubleshoot Windows OS problems

questions.scenarioText: A user's Windows 10 computer is infected with malware that prevents internet access.
questions.questionText: Which of the following commands can help identify network issues? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: ipconfig shows IP config; netstat shows active connections and ports.
explanation.incorrect: dir lists files; chkdsk checks disk.
explanation.examTip: netstat -an shows all connections in numeric form.

metadata.examObjective: 1.2: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: Evaluate each statement about Windows Registry.

statements.text: Registry contains configuration settings for Windows.
Registry editing is recommended for daily use.
Registry backups should be made before making changes.
Registry includes HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE and HKEY_CURRENT_USER.

explanation.correct: Registry stores config; editing can be risky; always backup; hives include HKLM and HKCU.
explanation.incorrect: Registry editing should be done cautiously.
explanation.examTip: Export a registry key before editing it.

metadata.examObjective: 1.2: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: Which Windows feature is used to prevent unauthorized access to files and folders?

explanation.correct: NTFS permissions control access to files and folders.
explanation.incorrect: Windows Defender is antivirus; Task Scheduler schedules tasks; PowerShell is scripting.
explanation.examTip: NTFS permissions include Read, Write, and Full Control.

metadata.examObjective: 1.8: Compare and contrast Windows file system and storage

questions.scenarioText: You are tasked with automating a repetitive task on a Windows server.
questions.questionText: Which scripting languages are commonly used for Windows automation? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Batch and PowerShell are native to Windows.
explanation.incorrect: Bash is Linux; Python is cross-platform but not native.
explanation.examTip: PowerShell is more powerful and modern than Batch.

metadata.examObjective: 1.12: Given a scenario, use the appropriate scripting language

questions.questionText: Order the steps to use Disk Cleanup in Windows.

orderItems.text: Open Disk Cleanup and select the drive
Select file types to delete (temporary files, etc.)
Click OK to delete the files
Confirm deletion

explanation.correct: 1: Open Disk Cleanup, 2: Select files, 3: OK, 4: Confirm.
explanation.incorrect: Skipping confirmation could delete important files.
explanation.examTip: Disk Cleanup helps free up space on the system drive.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are features of Windows 11? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Windows 11 supports Android apps and Snap Layouts.
explanation.incorrect: Internet Explorer is deprecated; Cortana is less prominent.
explanation.examTip: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0 and secure boot.

metadata.examObjective: 1.1: Compare and contrast Windows versions and features

questions.questionText: Evaluate each statement about Windows File Explorer.

statements.text: File Explorer supports file search.
File Explorer can map network drives.
File Explorer does not show file extensions by default.
File Explorer can create compressed folders.

explanation.correct: File Explorer supports search, mapping, and compressed folders.
explanation.incorrect: File Explorer does show extensions if enabled.
explanation.examTip: Enable 'File name extensions' in the View tab.

metadata.examObjective: 1.1: Compare and contrast Windows versions and features

questions.questionText: Match each Windows command to its function.

dragItems.text: System File Checker – verify system files

explanation.correct: chkdsk = disk check; sfc = system file check; diskpart = partition; ipconfig = IP config.
explanation.incorrect: Mismatching commands and functions.
explanation.examTip: sfc /scannow is used to repair system files.

metadata.examObjective: 1.2: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.scenarioText: A user cannot log in to their Windows 10 workstation after entering an incorrect password multiple times.
questions.questionText: Which of the following actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Reset the user's password using the administrator account
Unlock the user account in Active Directory

explanation.correct: Reset password via admin; unlock account in AD if domain-joined.
explanation.incorrect: Restarting doesn't fix account lockouts; reinstall is extreme.
explanation.examTip: Account lockout policies can cause this.

metadata.examObjective: 1.4: Given a scenario, troubleshoot Windows OS problems

questions.questionText: Order the steps to perform a malware removal in Windows.

orderItems.text: Isolate the system from the network
Run antivirus/anti-malware scan
Remove/quarantine detected malware
Update antivirus and re-scan

explanation.correct: 1: Isolate, 2: Scan, 3: Remove, 4: Update and re-scan.
explanation.incorrect: Isolation prevents spread.
explanation.examTip: Always update malware definitions before scanning.

metadata.examObjective: 2.4: Given a scenario, use the appropriate security practices

questions.questionText: Which of the following are valid PowerShell commands? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Get-Process and Get-Service are valid cmdlets.
explanation.incorrect: List-Process and Show-Service are not native.
explanation.examTip: PowerShell cmdlets follow Verb-Noun pattern.

metadata.examObjective: 1.12: Given a scenario, use the appropriate scripting language

questions.questionText: Evaluate each statement about Windows Task Manager.

statements.text: Task Manager can end processes.
Task Manager shows CPU and memory usage.
Task Manager can manage startup programs.
Task Manager can change system settings.

explanation.correct: Task Manager ends processes, shows usage, manages startup.
explanation.incorrect: Task Manager cannot change system settings.
explanation.examTip: Use Task Manager to quickly check system performance.

metadata.examObjective: 1.2: Given a scenario, use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: Order the steps to create a new user account in Windows.

orderItems.text: Open Settings or Control Panel
Select 'Add new user'
Enter username and password
Select account type (standard/administrator)

explanation.correct: 1: Open Settings, 2: Add user, 3: Credentials, 4: Account type.
explanation.incorrect: Account type determines permissions.
explanation.examTip: Minimize administrative account usage.

questions.questionText: Match each backup type to its restore complexity.

dragItems.text: Most complex restore – full + all incrementals

explanation.correct: Full=1 set; Incremental=full+all incrementals; Differential=full+latest diff.
explanation.incorrect: Misunderstanding restore complexity.
explanation.examTip: Differential restores are simpler than incremental.

questions.questionText: Which Windows utility is used to manage disk partitions?

explanation.correct: Disk Management is used to create, format, and manage partitions.
explanation.incorrect: Device Manager handles hardware; Task Scheduler schedules tasks; Registry Editor edits registry.
explanation.examTip: Diskpart is the command-line alternative.

questions.scenarioText: You are configuring a Windows 11 workstation for a developer who needs to run Linux containers.
questions.questionText: Which features should be enabled? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: WSL 2 and Hyper-V allow running Linux containers.
explanation.incorrect: Windows Sandbox is for testing; BitLocker is encryption.
explanation.examTip: WSL 2 is more compatible with Docker.

questions.questionText: Evaluate each statement about Group Policy.

statements.text: Group Policy is used to manage settings in Active Directory.
Group Policy can be applied to local computers only.
Group Policy can enforce password policies.
Group Policy is available in Windows Home edition.

explanation.correct: Group Policy manages AD settings, enforces security, not in Home edition.
explanation.incorrect: Group Policy can be applied to domain and local.
explanation.examTip: gpedit.msc is the local Group Policy Editor.

questions.questionText: Order the steps to enable BitLocker on a Windows system.

orderItems.text: Open BitLocker Drive Encryption from Control Panel
Select the drive to encrypt
Choose how to unlock the drive (password, smart card, etc.)
Start encryption and wait for completion

explanation.correct: 1: Open BitLocker, 2: Select drive, 3: Unlock method, 4: Encrypt.
explanation.incorrect: Backup the recovery key before encrypting.
explanation.examTip: BitLocker requires TPM for maximum security.

questions.questionText: Select the correct Windows version for each feature.

explanation.correct: BitLocker, Hyper-V, and Sandbox are in Pro editions.

explanation.correct: cp copies files; mv moves/renames files.
explanation.incorrect: delete and remove are not standard Linux commands.
explanation.examTip: rm is used to remove files in Linux.

statements.text: Windows Update can install security patches.
Windows Update can update drivers.
Windows Update can upgrade to a newer version.
Windows Update cannot be paused.

explanation.correct: Windows Update can install patches, drivers, and upgrades.
